paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: comparison by language family.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates a comparison of morphosyntactic probing performance across different language families, specifically representing the task count where specific models performed better or yielded the same results. The horizontal category axis lists the language families in alphabetical order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical value axis is labeled "task count" and uses a linear scale with a value range from 0 to 40, displaying numeric tick labels and corresponding horizontal grid lines at regular intervals of 10. For each language family on the horizontal axis, the chart displays a grouped set of up to three vertical bars. According to the legend titled "better," the bars denote which outcome was superior: light blue bars represent the "mBERT" model, dark blue bars represent the "XLM-R" model, and light green bars represent "same." All bars are drawn with a thin black outline. The tallest bar on the chart belongs to the XLM-R category in the IE-Slavic group, reaching an approximate task count of 39. In contrast, the lowest values occur where bars are entirely absent, indicating a count of 0 for mBERT in both the IE-Baltic and Semitic groups. The shortest visible bars indicate a task count of approximately 1, as seen for mBERT in the IE-Indic, IE-other, Isolate, and Uralic groups, as well as for the "same" category in the Isolate and Semitic groups. Other notable bar heights include the "same" category in IE-Romance reaching 30, and the XLM-R category in IE-Germanic at approximately 18.
